visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A close-up image of a cheek with red and brown spots serves as the background. In the foreground, a female doctor with short brown hair and glasses, wearing a brown-and-white striped shirt, points to the skin spots. (2) The background shifts to a modern office setting with a desk, bookshelf, and lamps. The woman speaks to the camera while gesturing with her hands to her face. (3) A split-screen before-and-after photo of acne-scarred skin appears behind her. She uses her hands to indicate the transition from scarred to smooth skin. (4) Back in the office, she holds up three fingers and then gestures upward as a block of text listing ingredients appears. (5) She makes a surprised or comical face while gesturing broadly with her hands, followed by heart emojis popping up around her head. (6) She points upward again, and an image of a 'DRX Vitamin C' bottle appears in the center, followed by a 'DRX Sunscreen' bottle. She makes a spreading motion with her hands to suggest application. (7) She continues her explanation, pointing to her palms and counting ingredients. Text labels for specific acids appear near her hands. (8) She waves her hands horizontally, indicating the disappearance of spots. (9) Multiple layers of bold yellow text appear across the screen as she makes an 'OK' sign with both hands and looks directly into the lens. (10) The video ends with a white background and the 'DRX Series Skincare' logo in the center.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: List-based: Misconception Clarification -> Evidence Presentation -> Ingredient Recommendations -> Practical Application Tips -> Final CTA.
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: To educate the audience on how to distinguish true acne scars from post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH) and to promote DRX skincare products as effective treatments for the latter.
